outline.chapter_title: The Landscape of Text-to-Image Diffusion and Adaptation
outline.description: This chapter provides the foundational context for the research, defining state-of-the-art diffusion models and identifying the critical gap in fine-tuning: balancing task-specific adaptation with the preservation of pre-trained semantic knowledge.
subtopics: Introduction to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models (Stable Diffusion, Imagen)
The Two Core Tasks: Subject-Driven Generation (DreamBooth) and Controllable Generation (ControlNet)
The Limits of Current Methods: Why Small Learning Rates and LoRA Fail
Defining Desiderata: Training Efficiency vs. Generalizability Preservation
The Measurement Problem: Why Euclidean Distance is Insufficient

outline.chapter_title: Why Neuron Angles Matter: The Physics of Deep Semantics
outline.description: This chapter delves into the theoretical underpinnings of fine-tuning, arguing that while magnitudes are stable, it is the angular relationships between neurons that encode semantic information within a neural network.
subtopics: Hyperspherical Similarity and Hyperuniformity in Neural Networks
Experimental Evidence: Angular Information vs. Magnitude in Autoencoders
The Complex Manifold Topology of Layer Neurons
Decoupling Semantics from Task-Specific Control via Direction Changes
Hyperspherical Energy as a Quantification Tool

outline.description: This chapter presents the core contributions of Orthogonal Finetuning, formally defining how to update model weights using orthogonal transformations to strictly preserve pairwise neuron angles.
subtopics: The Orthogonal Transformation Strategy: Preserving Pairwise Similarities
Formulating OFT: Minimizing Hyperspherical Energy Difference ($L=0$)
'Just Rotate': The Structural Constraint without Magnitude Change'
Intuitive Analogy: Phase Retrieval in 2D Fourier Transforms
From Theory to Practice: The Forward Pass Formula

outline.description: [Appendix/Deep Dive] This chapter addresses the computational challenges associated with enforcing orthogonal constraints. It details how standard methods are inefficient and introduces the specific optimizations used in OFT to make them feasible for large-scale diffusion models.
